evals.prompt: I'm creating a new Agent Skill that validates GraphQL schemas. Write the YAML frontmatter `description` field for its SKILL.md so it routes reliably.
assertions: The description starts with an imperative 'Use when' (or 'Use this skill when') phrasing rather than 'This skill...' / 'I can...' / 'You can...'.
The description contains an explicit trigger clause of the form 'even when the user doesn't say ...' (or equivalent 'even if not mentioned') to catch non-obvious matches.
The description contains NO negative/out-of-scope 'Skip ...' exclusion clause and does not point to any other skill by name.

evals.prompt: I'm authoring an Agent Skill about Docker. Create the reference file references/multi-stage-builds.md that goes deeper on multi-stage build patterns, with correct frontmatter and structure for a skill reference file.
assertions: The reference file contains NO YAML frontmatter block (no `name:`/`description:` header fenced by `---`).
The reference file body does NOT include any sentence telling the reader when or why to read this file itself (e.g. 'Read this when working with multi-stage builds').

evals.prompt: I'm writing references/error-handling.md for a Go coding-guideline skill. The content is distilled from Dave Cheney's blog posts and a GopherCon talk. Add the guidance to the reference file along with proper source attribution.
assertions: The reference file body does NOT name the author, blog, company, or talk inside references/error-handling.md.
Provenance/attribution is directed to a separate SOURCES.md file rather than embedded in the reference body.

evals.prompt: Draft the Essentials section of a SKILL.md for a new Rust coding-guideline skill covering ownership, error handling, and async. Each topic has its own reference file.
assertions: Each essentials bullet leads with a bolded short rule name followed by a brief (roughly 5-10 word) how-to.
Each essentials bullet cross-references its topic's references/*.md file via a markdown link (e.g. 'see [references/ownership.md](references/ownership.md)').

evals.prompt: Our planning command always needs plan-guide, but one operation can optionally use any installed changelog skill whose description fits. Explain how to represent both relationships without copying instructions or building another metadata catalog.
assertions: Places the exact plan-guide installation dependency in every supported plugin manifest and matching package dependencies.
Keeps optional changelog selection in runtime prose and selects from installed skill names and routing descriptions.
States that installation does not load a skill into context and avoids copying either skill's procedure.
Does not add lifecycle roles, provisions, semantic-version ranges, overlays, or another composition catalog.

evals.prompt: A workflow requires evidence review. Two installed skill descriptions fit equally well, and a third matching skill exists only in a remote marketplace. Resolve the required capability.
assertions: Reports the two installed description matches as ambiguous and does not choose by filesystem, marketplace, prompt, or version order.
Treats the required ambiguity as blocking until the caller selects or further distinguishes the need.
Does not select the remote-only skill because soft runtime selection is limited to installed skills.
